question: When reversible extremotolerance systems are aligned at stress exit (rehydration/germination = tau0), is complete molecular repair required before organismal/cellular function resumes?
measurement_rule: Use reported sampling windows and functional milestones. Do not invent exponential half-lives from sparse points.

systems.first_function: movement begins around ~5 min in a 2024 ultrastructural protocol
systems.interpretation: Fast behavioral re-entry does not establish complete molecular restoration.

systems.first_function: recovery measured at 2/6/24/48 h; cumulative activity rises over time
systems.interpretation: Recovery is distributed rather than instantaneous; older animals and longer/repeated dormancy show poorer/slower return.

systems.first_function: full mobility reported by ~8 h in one repair experiment
systems.early_repair: DNA-repair/oxidoreduction response peaks early (~1.5 h in later transcriptomic study); PFGE repair tracked 0/2/8/24/48 h
systems.molecular_repair_complete: DSB signal can remain at 48 h despite restored mobility

systems.first_function: larvae can revive rapidly, classically within ~1 h
systems.early_repair: rehydration produces severe oxidative damage; a 2023 study reports DNA/protein/lipid oxidation repaired within a couple of hours
systems.molecular_repair_complete: older DSB assays report genome-integrity recovery on a longer ~96-h scale
systems.interpretation: Functional return and different molecular repair layers have different time constants.

systems.early_repair: predamaged-spore work places important lesion processing during early revival, including ~15-60 min ripening/outgrowth windows
systems.replication_constraint: repair/checkpoint defects delay outgrowth and increase mutation/chromosome segregation defects during first replication
systems.interpretation: Strongest evidence that dangerous restart processes are damage-gated, but not proof that every cellular function waits for total repair.

systems.state_reset: 24-h rehydrated transcriptome clusters close to hydrated control
systems.physiology: photosynthetic carbon assimilation substantially recovers by ~48 h
systems.interpretation: Recovery is a staged transition across molecular and physiological layers.

revised_survivor.name: STAGED_DAMAGE_AWARE_REENTRY
revised_survivor.formula: PROTECTED_STATE -> REHYDRATE/GERMINATE -> EARLY_SENSING_AND_REPAIR -> LOW_RISK_FUNCTIONS_CAN_RETURN -> DAMAGE_CHECKPOINTS_GATE_HIGH_RISK_RESTART -> CONTINUED_REPAIR_AND_NORMALIZATION -> FULL_STABLE_STATE
revised_survivor.key_point: There is not one universal EXIT time. Different layers—movement, metabolism, transcription, genome integrity, replication and full physiology—can recover on distinct timescales.
revised_survivor.relation_to_longevity_survivor: Adds an ordering principle: safe recovery may depend on gating specific high-risk functions to damage state, rather than demanding complete repair of everything before any activity resumes.
revised_survivor.claim_ceiling: Cross-kingdom survival abstraction only; not a mammalian rejuvenation mechanism.

next_tests: For each reversible extremophile, measure separate tau50 values for behavioral function, metabolic function, genome integrity, proteome oxidation, replication/growth and full physiology only when quantitative curves exist.
Test whether replication/growth tau is more tightly coupled to genome-repair completion than movement or basic metabolism across at least three independent lineages.
Use Bacillus checkpoint mutants as a causal positive control and Adineta as a counterexample to total-repair-first models.
Seek modern rehydration omics for Chroococcidiopsis to prospectively test the staged-reentry model.
